item.title: Volume 9, Number 3, October 2013
item.description:
Constraint Programming News

Editor: Guido Tack

Editorial

You may have noticed that there have not been any updates to the Constraint Programming News since the beginning of the year. Our previous editors, Jimmy Lee, Eric Monfroy, and Toby Walsh handed their duties over to the ACP EC after many years of service to the community. We would like to thank them for the great effort and time they put in to keep us all up to date!

item.title: Volume 10, Number 1, April 2014
item.description:
Constraint Programming News

Editors:

Guido Tack, Pedro Meseguer, Pierre Schaus, Roland Yap

CONTENTS

  • editorial
  • news: ACP report
  • papers with impact (by Gilles Pesant)
  • other news: publications, jobs, events

Editorial

This is the second issue of CP News for 2014.

As always, we have the latest updates from the ACP Executive Committee. There are a few close deadlines in the report, such as May 12 for proposing tutorials for CP 2014, May 18 for community input to the new Strategic Committee, and May 25 for applications to this year’s summer school.

item.description:

  • New initiative: Archiving CP-related PhD theses

Editorial

This is the combined issue 2 and 3 of CP News for 2014.

In this issue, you find the latest news from the ACP Executive Committee (as usual). Two items to highlight: the results of the ACP EC elections have been published, and the EC is still looking for proposals to host the 2015 ACP Summer School.

item.description:

CONTENTS

  • editorial
  • news: ACP report for Q4 2014
  • Constraints journal: Now publishing thesis abstracts
  • Papers with impact (by Jean-François Puget)

Editorial

Welcome to the first issue of the Constraint Programming Newsletter for 2015.

Reminder: You have to renew your membership if you want to remain a member of the ACP. Not a member yet? It’s easy to sign up!

In this issue we can announce a new initiative of the ACP and the Constraints journal, publishing annual collections of thesis abstracts. Furthermore, we have the third article in our series on classic papers with impact.
